_note: What Masa, Kawasemi-yu's keeper, says when the farmer talks to her (Talk, README.md, Villagers): the first pick whose if holds names the lines, one of them by the day; at her counter the keeper's ask comes first (data/shops.json sento ask) and Talk gives one of these. The gift_ lines answer a gift by its reaction; gift_items names her own answer to a keepsake or a dish (Talk.gift_line), by item or by dish:<reaction> (gifts in data/villagers/masa.json). She has no hearts, so no band rows past the first meeting. Our own lines.

lines.speaker: masa
lines.text: Still here? The water won't get any hotter with you watching me.

lines.speaker: masa
lines.text: Go on, have a soak. Talking is free, but the bath is better.

lines.speaker: masa
lines.text: So you're the new farmer. I'm Masa. I've kept Kawasemi-yu since before the bridge got its new boards.

lines.speaker: masa
lines.text: Wash before you get in, keep your towel out of the water, and you and I will get along fine.

lines.speaker: masa
lines.text: Kawasemi-yu, two in the afternoon till eleven. Thursdays I rest my back. So does the boiler.

lines.speaker: masa
lines.text: The bath's shut today. Even the boiler gets to see the blossoms once a year.

lines.speaker: masa
lines.text: When I was a girl the lanterns floated past the bath. We'd all lean out of the window, wet hair and all.

lines.speaker: masa
lines.text: A moon like that and no bath open. I'll have a late soak when I get home, keeper's privilege.

lines.speaker: masa
lines.text: First bath of the year is the best one. Come early, before the water gets crowded.

lines.speaker: masa
lines.text: Thursday. No firewood, no counter, no wet floors. I just sit and watch the river do the work.

lines.speaker: masa
lines.text: Rainy days the whole village remembers the bath. Bring a dry towel, the one in your basket won't be.

lines.speaker: masa
lines.text: Morning's for the boiler. Oak burns long, cedar burns fast, and my back hates both.

lines.speaker: masa
lines.text: Almost closing. The last bather always says just five more minutes. I give them ten.

lines.speaker: masa
lines.text: In summer they come for the cold milk more than the hot water. I don't mind. Milk pays too.

lines.speaker: masa
lines.text: Snow on the roof and steam on the windows. This is when a bathhouse earns its keep.

lines.speaker: masa
lines.text: Walk home quick after your bath tonight, or the cold will undo all my good work.

lines.speaker: masa
lines.text: My husband painted the mountain on the bath wall. He got the river wrong. I never told him.

lines.speaker: masa
lines.text: Farmers make the best bathers. You come in tired and go out new. That's the whole job, really.

lines.speaker: masa
lines.text: The milk's in the cooler, the coins go on the counter. I keep count better than you'd think.

lines.speaker: masa
lines.text: For me? You know the way to an old woman's heart, don't you. Thank you.

lines.speaker: masa
lines.text: That's thoughtful of you. I'll have it after closing.

lines.speaker: masa
lines.text: Well, thank you. I'll find a use for it.

lines.speaker: masa
lines.text: Hm. Not really to my taste, but it's the thought. Thank you.

lines.speaker: masa
lines.text: A rock? I have enough grit on my floors already, thank you.

lines.speaker: masa
lines.text: A fan! Just the thing behind a counter full of steam. You've a good eye.

lines.speaker: masa
lines.text: Home cooking, and warm too. I'll eat it at the counter between bathers. Thank you.

lines.speaker: masa
lines.text: A proper meal. Better than the rice ball I had planned.

lines.speaker: masa
lines.text: You cooked this? Good. A body that eats well soaks well. Thank you.

lines.speaker: masa
lines.text: Not my sort of dish, I'm afraid. The regulars might like it, though. Thank you.

lines.speaker: masa
lines.text: One gift a day is plenty. Save the rest for your bath fee.
